COM · Solved Past QuestionsMultiplexing IV: TDM numericals Q9 The figure shows synchronous TDM with a data stream for each input and one data stream for the output. The unit of data is 1 bit. Find (a) the input bit duration, (b) the output bit duration, (c) the output bit rate and (d) the output frame rate.BTCL AM(Technical) 2021 · JBL SO(ANE) 2020 1 Mbps1 Mbps1 Mbps1 Mbps TDM4 Mbps1 frame = 4 bits Figure (textbook version): four inputs at 1 Mbps.(a) input bit = 1/1 Mbps = 1 µs(b) output bit = 1/4 Mbps = 0.25 µs(c) output rate = 4 × 1 Mbps = 4 Mbps(d) frame rate = input rate = 1,000,000 frames/s Q10 Two channels, one at 190 kbps and the other at 180 kbps, are multiplexed using pulse-stuffing TDM with no synchronisation bits. Find (a) the frame size in bits, (b) the frame rate, (c) the frame duration and (d) the data rate.RAKUB ME 2021 → pulse stuffing raises the 180-kbps channel to 190 kbps · (a) 2 bits (1 per channel) · (b) 190,000 frames/s · (c) 1/190,000 = 5.26 µs · (d) 2 × 190 kbps = 380 kbps Q11 A TDMA system has 8 transmitter–receiver pairs. Each is sampled at 8 kHz, giving 16 bits per sample. Two synchronisation bits are added to each frame. Calculate the data rate of the TDMA link.BTCL AM(Technical) 2021 → frame = 8 × 16 + 2 = 130 bits; frames/s = 8000 → R = 130 × 8000 = 1.04 Mbps Q12 In a TDM system eight signals of 2 kHz each are sampled 25% above the Nyquist rate; the quantisation error must not exceed 1% of the signal amplitude. Find the bit rate (recalled wording).NESCO AM(ICT) 2021 → fs = 1.25 × 2 × 2 kHz = 5 kHz · error ≤ Δ/2 = 1% of peak mp, Δ = 2mp/L → L ≥ 100 → 128 levels, n = 7 · R = 8 × 5000 × 7 = 280 kbps Q13 How long does it take to send a file of 500,000 bits from host A to host B over a circuit-switched network where all links are 1.536 Mbps, each link uses TDM with 32 slots, and it takes 800 ms to establish the end-to-end circuit?Combined Bank AHE 2021 · also on the Petrobangla ANE suggestion sheet → one circuit = 1.536 Mbps ÷ 32 = 48 kbps · transfer = 500,000 ÷ 48,000 = 10.42 s · total = 10.42 + 0.8 = 11.22 s Exam trap A circuit gets one slot, i.e. 1/32 of the link, never the full 1.536 Mbps; and the set-up time is added once. Suggestion-sheet variant (16 slots, 1.5 Mbps, no set-up): 500,000 ÷ 93,750 = 5.33 s. 5

COM · Solved Past QuestionsShannon & Nyquist capacity Q21 A telephone line normally has a bandwidth of 3000 Hz (300 to 3300 Hz) assigned for data communication. The SNR is usually 3162. What will be the capacity of this channel?Combined Bank AP 2023 · RPGCL AM(ICT) 2022 → C = 3000 × log₂(1 + 3162) = 3000 × 11.63 = 34,881 bps ≈ 34.88 kbps (3162 = 35 dB) Exam trap One printed answer writes "SNR = 3162 dB": 3162 is the power ratio (= 35 dB). Putting 3162 dB into the formula is meaningless. Q22 Find the channel capacity of a teleprinter channel with 300 Hz bandwidth and an SNR of 3 dB.MRA AME 2022 → SNR = 100.3 = 1.995 → C = 300 × log₂(2.995) = 300 × 1.583 = 474.8 bps (one printed copy misprints 30 dB in the "given" line) Q23 For a noisy channel, the signal-to-noise power ratio is 0.1 and the bandwidth is 2.4 GHz. What is the channel capacity in Mbps?46th BCS ICT → C = 2.4 × 10⁹ × log₂(1.1) = 2.4 × 10⁹ × 0.1375 = 330 Mbps (SNR below 1 still gives capacity: spread-spectrum works this way) MCQAnswer a. Gaussian channel, SNR = 15, B = 16 kHz: C (kbps) = (a) 32 (b) 64 (c) 18 (d) 128 49th BCS ICT (2025)(b) 64 b. B = 1 MHz, SNR = 63: bit rate = (a) 4 Mbps (b) 6 Mbps (c) 8 Mbps (d) 10 Mbps BPSC AME 2019(b) 6 Mbps c. B = 200 kHz, 4 signal levels, max data rate: (a) 400 kbps (b) 800 kbps (c) 1000 kbps (d) 1200 kbps Combined Bank SO(IT) 2021(b) 800 kbps → (a) 16k × log₂16 = 64 kbps · (b) 1M × log₂64 = 6 Mbps · (c) Nyquist: 2 × 200k × log₂4 = 800 kbps Q24 Using the Nyquist theorem, a channel can be sampled 12 million times per second; four-level signals give 2 bits per sample. What is the total data rate? (6-MHz noiseless channel.)NESCO AM(ICT) 2021 → R = 2 × 6 MHz × log₂4 = 24 Mbps Q25 Signal power 10 mW, noise power 1 µW: find SNR and SNR in dB.MGMCL AM(ICT) 2022 → SNR = 10 × 10⁻³ / 10⁻⁶ = 10,000 → 10 log₁₀(10⁴) = 40 dB. Noiseless channel: SNR → ∞. 9

Show the resulting signal using (i) NRZ-L, (ii) Manchester, (iii) unipolar RZ.BPSC AE 2022 01001110 NRZ-L1 = +V, 0 = −V Manchester0 ↓ , 1 ↑ (802.3) Unipolar RZ1 = +V half bit Exam trap State your convention: some books draw NRZ-L with 0 = +V, and Manchester per G. Q42 A communication numerical on NRZ and RZ line coding (recalled wording).Teletalk Executive(Technical) 2015 → the usual ask is bandwidth for N bps: NRZ changes at most once per bit → Bmin ≈ N/2 (1 Mbps → 500 kHz); RZ and Manchester change twice per bit → Bmin ≈ N (1 Mbps → 1 MHz), the price of self-clocking. MCQAnswer a. 1110000100110101 in 4B/5B: max consecutive zeros in the output: (a) 1 (b) 4 (c) 2 (d) 3 BUET M.Sc. April 2021(d) 3 b. Read a differential Manchester waveform (figure not reproduced): (a) 10000111 (b) 01000100 (c) 01111000 (d) 10111011 BUET M.Sc. April 2021see the rule below → (a) 1110→11100, 0001→01001, 0011→10101, 0101→01011 → 11100 01001 10101 01011: longest run of 0s = 3 (4B/5B never allows more than 3). (b) Rule: a transition at the start of a bit = 0, no transition = 1; the mid-bit transition is only the clock. 16

Purpose: very wide channels → multi-Gbps rates and about 1 ms latency for dense device clusters; small antennas allow beam-forming arrays. Applications: 5G fixed wireless and backhaul, industrial IoT / smart factories, AR/VR, connected vehicles (V2X), high-resolution radar sensing. Limit: short range, blocked by walls and rain, so it needs dense small cells. COM · Solved Past QuestionsMobile II: TCSM, VoIP, CDMA, 5G Q66 What is the function of TCSM? What equipment is needed for VoIP? What is a call drop and what causes it? What are GPS, VoIP, CDMA and GSM, and why are they used?BTRC DAD 2021 · BTRC DAD(Technical) 2019 TCSM (transcoder and sub-multiplexer): converts the 13-kbps GSM speech (16 kbps with overhead) to 64-kbps PCM for the MSC, and packs four 16-kbps channels into one 64-kbps timeslot, saving transmission lines. VoIP equipment: IP phone or softphone / ATA adapter, broadband IP network with QoS, SIP server / IP-PBX (softswitch), VoIP gateway to the PSTN, codecs (G.711, G.729), router / firewall. Call drop = a call cut off before either user ends it. Causes: weak coverage, handover failure, interference, network congestion, faulty BTS / backhaul, high speed of the user, handset fault. GPS: satellite positioning (navigation, timing) · VoIP: voice over IP networks, cheap calls · CDMA: users share the band by codes · GSM: 2G digital cellular standard for voice and SMS. Q67 Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of TDMA and CDMA.46th BCS ICT TDMACDMA Advantagessimple, cheap handsets, battery saving (radio off in other slots), easy hand-offmore users per MHz, soft hand-off, resists interference and tapping, frequency reuse 1 Disadvantagesneeds strict sync and guard time, fixed slots wasted, multipath ISIneeds tight power control (near–far problem), complex receivers, capacity falls as load rises Q68 Identify the differences between 1G, 2G, 3G and 5G networks. Write the disadvantages of 5G in terms of initial cost and battery drainage.Fisheries & Livestock Instructor(CS) 2023 · Rupali Bank ANE 2021 GenTechnologySignal / accessSpeedService 1GAMPSanalog, FDMAvoice onlyvoice 2GGSM, IS-95digital, TDMA / CDMA9.6–64 kbpsvoice, SMS 3GUMTS / WCDMAWCDMA≈ 2 Mbps+video call, mobile Internet 5GNROFDM, mmWave, massive MIMOup to 20 Gbps, ≈ 1 mseMBB, IoT, URLLC 5G disadvantages: initial cost: dense small cells, fibre backhaul and new spectrum make roll-out very expensive; battery drainage: wide-band radios and many antennas use more power and heat, so phones drain faster, especially while searching between 4G and 5G. 26

COM · Solved Past QuestionsAlso filed here Q69 Write the differences between a digital telephone and a mobile phone. What is a modem? Write its uses.15th NTRCA Computer Operation (2019) Digital (fixed) telephone: wired to the exchange, fixed location, digital switching (ISDN / PCM), very stable. Mobile phone: wireless cellular link to a base station, moves with hand-over, needs a SIM and battery, adds SMS and data. Modem (modulator–demodulator) converts digital data to an analog signal for the line and back. Uses: dial-up / DSL / cable Internet, fax, GSM modems for SMS alerts, POS terminals, remote monitoring. Q70 Explain the parity method for error detection. Write the bit strings of "Delta" using ASCII.BB AME 2023 The sender adds one parity bit so the count of 1s is even (even parity) or odd (odd parity); the receiver recounts. It detects any odd number of flipped bits, never an even number, and cannot correct.
